solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parent (male) replaces second ring in engine

indicators.note: the male pronoun takes the place of the second ring-shaped letter in the engine word

parts.note: an engine is a motor
a ring is round like the letter O
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A mechanic's note about swapping a piston ring in an engine, with a stray bracket about a male parent.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTOR has two Os; 'replaces second' means only the later one gives way to HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is a female parent, so the word is a direct example of the definition.

clue.text: Foul vapours over Chad hiding a massively uneven contest

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
the single letter a is tucked away out of sight, so it drops out of the vapours word

parts.note: a miasma is a noxious, foul-smelling vapour
TCH is the international vehicle code for Chad

explanation.surface: A news line about poisonous fumes drifting over the African country of Chad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding a' removes one A from MIASMA, leaving MISMA; TCH (Chad) goes below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly unequal pairing of competitors is a contest where the sides do not match.

clue.text: Solitary order to free on a motion

indicators.note: a motion is movement, so the letters of the fodder are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A committee minute: a proposal to release someone, put to the meeting as a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' looks like a meeting's formal proposal, but it stirs up TO FREE ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot of tea for one person is what a lone café customer orders, a solitary order.

clue.text: Point to rising total of birds

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word is read from the bottom up, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A bird count where someone points at the climbing tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point here, not a gesture; in a down clue 'rising' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds, an example of the plural definition.

clue.text: Shop around for announced light source

indicators.note: the letters of the shop word are moved around into a fresh order
announced means spoken, so the next piece is a word as it sounds rather than as written

parts.note: the little word for, said out loud, gives a sound spelt here with PH

explanation.surface: Someone shopping around for a lamp that has been advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' looks like 'advertised', but it marks the sound of 'for', whose spelling here borrows PH from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A phosphor is a substance that glows when energised, used to give light in screens and lamps.

clue.text: Clearance boss pulling up dock

parts.note: the head is the boss of an organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue pulling something up reads it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

explanation.surface: A harbour scene: the boss is pulling a boat up at the quay and checking the clearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling up' turns MOOR into ROOM, placed under HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is the vertical space overhead, the gap above something before it touches a ceiling or bridge.

clue.text: Iron held by parliamentary district at no time bringing complaint

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode district holding Parliament, written with I for the figure 1

indicators.note: the iron symbol is held, enclosed, by the letters of the never word

parts.note: never means at no time
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Westminster's iron grip never loosens, bringing endless complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postcode of Westminster, where Parliament sits; its figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine fever is an animal disease, and complaint is a standard word for an illness.

clue.text: Player for Scottish team gets a red card

definitions.meaning: ... (... of Midlothian) is an Edinburgh football club, so one of its players is a ...
... is one of the two red suits in playing cards, so one of its cards is a ...

explanation.surface: A footballer from a Scottish club is sent off by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red card' suggests a referee's sending-off, but it is a playing card of a red suit. Heart of Midlothian is an Edinburgh football club known as Hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a member of Heart of Midlothian, and a playing card from the red hearts suit.

clue.text: Live to be partial again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to side with someone is to be partial to them

explanation.surface: A question whether living means choosing a side once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful split of the answer into a prefix and a verb meaning take sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, a more formal synonym for dwelling.

clue.text: Georgia put up billionaire

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: The state of Georgia put up money for a very rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like 'funded', but 'up' alone reverses in a down clue, and 'put' is the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Gates, the Microsoft founder, is a famous example of a billionaire.

clue.text: Tool ejected to bend metal back

parts.note: spat, as in spat out, means ejected from the mouth
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter

indicators.note: back means the metal symbol is read in the other direction

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal

explanation.surface: A workshop tool shot out of a press to bend metal back into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AL into LA, which closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed utensil used for spreading or lifting, so it is a kind of tool.

clue.text: Brutes slam in a backhand

indicators.note: a backhand writes the other way, so the letters of the three words are read backwards

explanation.surface: A tennis player smashes the ball home with a backhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backhand' sounds like a tennis stroke; it reverses SLAMINA. 'slam' is fodder, not a tennis smash.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutes and animals are both creatures without human reason; brute is an old synonym for beast.

clue.text: One-time order for type of bomb

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
OM is the Order of Merit, a British order

explanation.surface: A former military command calling for a particular kind of bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' looks like 'former', but it splits into A and T. OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The atom bomb, an atomic weapon, is named after the particle, so the word identifies a kind of bomb.

clue.text: Aligned anew, put off about … about … about … about … about … about the onset of influenza

indicators.note: the second about means the reversed word goes around everything built by the later abouts
the first about turns the put off word round, reading it backwards

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off

indicators.note: the fourth about means the on piece wraps round what follows it

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: the sixth about means the re piece wraps round the influenza letter

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a business letter

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone driven to distraction by the endless ellipses of a rambling influenza report.
explanation.walkthrough: The six 'about's do three jobs: the first reverses, two give synonyms, three are containers. Built from the inside out: RIE, then ORIEN, then RETED wrapped round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reoriented means turned to face a new direction, which is the same as being lined up again.

clue.text: Speaking to a theologian, scripture seems in the end to be musical

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
RE, religious education, is the school subject of scripture

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the seems word

parts.note: to sing is to be musical with the voice

explanation.surface: A churchman notes that scripture, in the end, is meant to be sung.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, the British school subject once called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressing someone means directing your words at them, the same as talking to them.

clue.text: Surrounded by idiots, guru at last becomes opaque

indicators.note: the guru's letter is surrounded by, set inside, the idiots word

parts.note: clods are dull, stupid people

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the guru word

explanation.surface: A wise man amid fools finally loses his clarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes U from guru, which goes inside CLODS.
explanation.definitionFit: When glass or a liquid clouds over, it loses its clearness and stops being see-through.

clue.text: After a short time, even arsenic starts to seem horribly addictive

indicators.note: after means the remaining pieces follow, coming behind, the short time

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a short time

indicators.note: even picks the letters in the even positions of the arsenic word
starts to means the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A poisoning tale: after a moment even arsenic starts to feel like a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of arsenic, REI; 'starts to' takes S and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreish is British informal for food so tasty you keep wanting more, so it is addictive.

clue.text: Maybe cat's milk could make us careful

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the fodder may be made into something else

explanation.surface: A warning that pouring milk for the cat should make us careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: a cat's milk usually comes in a saucer.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucerful is the amount a saucer holds, and milk for a cat is typically served in one.

clue.text: Government-administered students get up to eat spud

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the students word encloses the spud word
in a down clue getting up reads the students word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students
tater is informal for a potato, like spud

explanation.surface: Students rise to tuck into a potato.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students; 'get up' in a down clue turns it upwards, giving SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A state-run body is managed by the government, the same as being administered by it.

clue.text: Hid that old surgeon smoked perhaps

parts.note: BS, Bachelor of Surgery, is a surgeon's qualification
smoking is one way of curing meat or fish, an example

explanation.surface: A tale of a former surgeon who hid his smoking habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says smoked is just one example of cured.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to hide it from view, so obscured is a past-tense synonym of hid.

clue.text: Confidential data showing ship passing island back to front

indicators.note: the ship's letters pass round either side of the island, enclosing it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: back to front moves the island's last letter round to its front

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Secret intelligence about a vessel sailing past a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' here moves only the island's final letter to its start, rather than reversing the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrets are pieces of information kept hidden from others, which is confidential data.

clue.text: Stun no-good, holding opponents at bay to start with

indicators.note: the no-good word holds the opponents inside it

parts.note: bum is slang for a worthless, no-good person
E and N are opposing seats at bridge, east facing north's side

indicators.note: to start with picks the first letter of the bay word

explanation.surface: A villain stuns his foes while holding them at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To benumb is to make numb or deaden the senses, which is to stun.

clue.text: Interfere in brawl about monkeys, the last being lost

indicators.note: about means the trimmed brawl word goes round the monkeys
the final letter of the brawl word is lost, dropped

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl
a monkey is British slang for 500 pounds, and D is the Roman numeral 500, so two of them give two Ds

explanation.surface: A zookeeper intervenes in a scrap among monkeys, one of which goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last being lost' trims the brawl to MELE. A 'monkey' is British slang for £500, and D is the Roman numeral 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to involve yourself in matters that are none of your business, to interfere.

clue.text: Very American composer

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
USA, as in made in the USA, labels something American

explanation.surface: Praise for a thoroughly American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Very American suggests the definition, but only composer defines: John Philip Sousa, the US march king.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was an American composer famous for military marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Public display of old site

parts.note: ex- means former, old
a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: An exhibition held at a former venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a large public exhibition, such as a world's fair, so it is a public display.

clue.text: Musician has piano in support

indicators.note: in means the piano letter sits inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician with a piano propped on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or a pipe, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: The elite return without a business-class car

indicators.note: without means the letter a is left out
return means the elite word is turned back to read in reverse

parts.note: the cream of society is its elite

explanation.surface: The elite go home without a luxury company car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CREAM into MAERC; 'without a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merc is British informal for a Mercedes-Benz, a car often used by executives.

clue.text: Daughter with beard in the early morning

parts.note: d is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or wheat

explanation.surface: A daughter with a beard first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is not on a face: an awn is the bristle on a grain such as barley.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, the very start of the morning.

clue.text: Over-embarrassed about irrational running back and forth being comparatively silly

indicators.note: about means the reversed blush goes round the middle pieces
over means turned over, so the embarrassed word reads backwards

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red

indicators.note: running back means the irrational number is first read in reverse, then forth, forwards

parts.note: pi is an irrational number
pi again, read forth, forwards this time

explanation.surface: An overly flustered person running back and forth is being sillier than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns RED into DER; 'running back and forth' gives PI backwards then forwards, IPPI, which DER goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dippy is informal for foolish or scatty, and the comparative form means more silly.

clue.text: Harder to replace one with a permanent employee

indicators.note: the letter a is set to replace the one letter in the harder word

parts.note: stiffer means harder, less bendy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It is harder to replace a single staff member with a new permanent hire.
explanation.walkthrough: In STIFFER, I (one) becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: A staffer is a member of an organisation's regular staff rather than a freelance or temp.

clue.text: Infuriating US gun enthusiasts with drink, say, all around

indicators.note: the say letters go all around the gun group and the drink

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
the NRA is the National Rifle Association, the US gun lobby
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: American gun fans drinking all round makes for an infuriating scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The NRA is the National Rifle Association, the US gun lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enraging makes people furious, so it is a synonym of infuriating.

clue.text: Cornered film director doesn't finish day

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the director's name is missing

parts.note: Ang Lee is a film director, maker of Brokeback Mountain

explanation.surface: A film director, trapped, can't finish his day's shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ang Lee is the Taiwanese-born director; 'doesn't finish' cuts his name to ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angled means having corners or set at an angle, as cornered does when describing a shape.
